thread:
Ava: Quick sync — we need a short triage to slim down the post-deploy backlog and decide what's shipped in the 2-week hotfix sprint. Proposing criteria below and asking for owners by EOD. Key asks: streaming latency regressions, webhook retries failing for customers, and a UX polish request from trial users. Thoughts? @Sam @Maria @Kevin @Jo

Sam: Agree. Suggest grouping by customer-impact + rollback risk. My quick rubric: P0/P1/P2/P3 (see code). I'll own streaming regression.

Kevin: UX polish looks like a cosmetic change; push to next cycle unless it's blocking onboarding flow.

Maria: Support tickets — three paying customers reported webhook retry loss (T-4821, T-4890, T-4912). One trial user flagged confusing error text. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/T-4821 https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/T-4890 https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/T-4912

Jo: SRE concern — if we backport hotfix to Dedicated, we'll need migration window and canary. Also, what SLA class should trigger immediate rollback?

Ava: Plan: 48h triage doc, owners assigned, dev spike if needed, ship hotfix mid-week. Canary policy: 5% -> 25% -> full. Prioritization rubric:

```
P0: production outage / data loss
P1: regression affecting >5% active users or revenue-impacting customers
P2: single-customer but high revenue/contractual impact
P3: enhancements, design polish, non-blocking
```

Also add quick checklist:
- owner, estimate (dev + QA), backport? (yes/no), canary window.

deploy-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary-1807654321 -> 5% -> monitor 2h.

Sam: I'll take streaming regression + webhook retry tickets. @Ava I'll post owners in the triage doc by EOD. :thumbsup:

Ava: thanks — I'll create the triage doc and shared board. Let's avoid scope creep: anything that requires >3 dev-days goes to next sprint unless it's P0/P1.
